===REPORT.md (uncommitted)===
# Rung M: `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing` for the compiler world

problem: `explorations/compile-ladder/after/raw/tests/oddJuxt.fss.compile:2` — "Function Nothing is not defined."; 472 further occurrences of "Maybe is undefined." across the ladder's recorded first errors, and the compiler prelude declares none of the three names.
spec: `Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:33-55` — the Convenience Types section declares `trait Maybe[\T\] comprises { Nothing, Just[\T\] }` with `isNothing: Boolean`, `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}`, and `object Just[\T\](just: T) extends Maybe[\T\]`; used at `Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:112-130`, which writes the defaults of two `Maybe` fields as `= Nothing`.
precedent: `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661` with bodies at `.fss:1308-1367` — the shipped `value trait Option[\E19\] extends { Condition[\E19\] } comprises { NoneObject[\E19\], Some[\E19\] }` with `coerce(_: None)` and `value object None end`, which is this protocol under other names and is the shape copied member for member; the team's own commented draft for these names is `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`.
deviation: eight, each listed in §6 below; the first is that the specification's single non-parametric `Nothing` is realised as `NothingObject[\T\]` plus `value object Nothing end` plus `coerce(_: Nothing)`, because a `where` clause on an object declaration is refused by `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4088` (`forObjectDeclPrePass`, `header.getWhereClause().isNone()`), while coercion is the one mechanism this path has and the interpreter lacks.

## 1. What was inherited

Nothing. `git log --oneline cb242a2d8..HEAD` was empty and `git status --short` clean when this rung started, so there was no earlier attempt to verify; `tmp/` held no logs. Every check below was run in this worktree.

## 2. Where does this fix belong

`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:332` is the `Maybe` row: interpreter at `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:813-880`, compiler world "present at `CompilerLibrary.fsi:194-204` but wholly commented out; `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:648-660` ships `Option`/`Some`/`NoneObject` instead". The row's spec column names `library/default-libraries.tex`, which is an api rendering and therefore not evidence (`Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31`); the governing prose is `basic-lib/convenience.tex`, found by grepping the prose chapters (§3).

The declarations belong in the library, not in the compiler. `grep -rn` over `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler` and `runtimeSystem` for `Option`, `Some`, `None` and `NoneObject` finds nothing, so the protocol this copies is special-cased nowhere in Java or Scala; and `WellKnownNames.java:114-115` makes `CompilerLibrary` and `CompilerBuiltin` the compile path's implicit prelude, so a declaration in either is in scope for every compiled program. This rung therefore touches no `.java` and no `.scala`, and needs no `ant compileAll`.

Within the library, the choice was `Library/CompilerLibrary` (where the team's draft sits) over `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin` (where `Option` sits). The draft's location was followed. It works: `CompilerLibrary` already declares objects that extend a trait declared in `CompilerBuiltin` (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:66-103`, thirteen objects extending `UncheckedException`, which is `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:711`), which is exactly what `Maybe extends Condition[\T\]` needs, and the coercion works from there (§5). It also costs less to rebuild: editing `CompilerLibrary` rebuilds three components (41 s + 2 s + 2 s measured), editing `CompilerBuiltin` would rebuild five (145 s measured cold).

## 3. Precedent search: has the team solved this here already, and in how many ways

Four ways, and they do not all agree.

1. **The interpreter's prelude.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1306-1364`: `value trait Maybe[\T\] extends { AnyMaybe, Condition[\T\], UniqueItem[\T\] } comprises { Nothing[\T\], Just[\T\] }`, `value object Just[\T\](x:T)` at `:1312`, `value object Nothing[\T\]` at `:1341`, `value trait AnyMaybe` at `:1292`, api at `.fsi:829-880`. The empty case is **parametric**, and the source says so under protest: `FortressLibrary.fss:1339-1340` "Obviously ought to be a non-parametric singleton when we get where clauses working", repeated in the api at `.fsi:857-858`.
2. **The team's draft for this world**, commented out at `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`: `value trait Maybe[\T\] extends Condition[\T\] comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(x: Nothing)`, `value object Just[\T\](x:T)`, `value object NothingObject[\T\]` with a second `coerce(x: Nothing)`, and `object Nothing end`. The empty case is **non-parametric plus a per-`T` object joined by a coercion**.
3. **The team's tests of that draft**, all in `ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/` and gated by nothing (`explorations/coordinator/map/test-coverage.md:32`): `MaybeTest1.fss:22-83`, `MaybeTest2.fss:29-`, `GenTest3.fss:29-41`, `GenTest4.fss:423-454`, `HelperTest1.fss:231-298` and its two copies — six components, all with `NothingObject[\T\]` and a separate `Nothing`, i.e. shape 2. `GenTest4.fss:454` writes it `value object Nothing end`; `MaybeTest1.fss:83` and `HelperTest1.fss:298` write `object Nothing end`.
4. **The shipped `Option`**, `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661` and `.fss:1308-1367`: shape 2 exactly, under the names `Option`, `Some`, `NoneObject`, `None`, complete, compiled into every program's prelude, and the only one of the four that is known to work. Nothing in the gated corpora names it (`grep -rn` over `compiler_tests/`, `other_compiler_tests/`, `library_tests/` finds only the English word "None" in three `Compiled12.*` files), so `probes/OptionCoercion.fss` was written to measure it before copying it. It compiles, links and runs: `probes/OptionCoercion.txt` records `empty=None full=Some(7)` / `PASS` for `empty: Option[\ZZ32\] = None`.

The corpus is a fifth voice but not a solution: every one of the 80 uses of the name in `ProjectFortress/tests/` and the `*_tests/` directories writes the parametric `Nothing[\T\]` (22 files; 15 of them in `tests/`), and so do `Library/List.fss` (4), `Set.fss` (6), `Map.fss` (11), `PureList.fss` (6) and `QuickCheck.fss`/`.fsi` — the interpreter-world library the later library route would port. There is no use of an unparameterised `Nothing` as a value anywhere in the tree outside shapes 2 and 3.

Shape 4 was copied, member for member, because it is the one that runs, and the names were taken from shape 2, because it is the team's decision for this world and it agrees with the specification (§4).

## 4. The decision

**The specification's spelling of the empty case was taken, not the corpus's.** `Maybe[\T\] comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(_: Nothing) = NothingObject[\T\]` and a separate `value object Nothing end`. This was a decision; it was not forced by the code.

The two candidates cannot coexist. `Nothing` is one name: either it is a non-parametric object, in which case `Nothing[\ZZ32\]` is a static error, or it is a parametric one, in which case a bare `Nothing` has no static argument to take. A same-name overload of the two is not merely unprecedented but unwritable: the coercion's parameter type has to name the singleton's type, and if a parametric object shares the name then the bare type name `Nothing` does not resolve to the singleton. So the fork is binary.

**What the specification says.** `basic-lib/convenience.tex:46-55` is a prose chapter of Part Basic Library, not an api rendering, and it declares the empty case as one object: `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}`. `basic/exceptions.tex:122,124` then uses it the way a non-parametric singleton is used, `getter message(): Maybe[\String\] = Nothing`. Two independent prose passages, and they agree.

**Why the specification's own text cannot be transcribed.** The declaration depends on a `where` clause, and the compile path refuses one on an object declaration: `CodeGen.java:4088`, in `forObjectDeclPrePass`, admits a declaration only if `header.getWhereClause().isNone()`, otherwise `sayWhat`. `probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss` is the specification's declaration under local names, and `probes/WhereClauseNothing.txt` records what happens to it. The compensating mechanism is coercion, which this path has and the interpreter does not (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:288`: "nothing: no occurrence of `Coercion` or `coerce` anywhere under `interpreter/`"). That is precisely why the team's draft for this world spells the empty case as it does, and why the interpreter's prelude does not: the interpreter had no way to write it.

**What the corpus says, and what it costs to overrule it.** Overruling it costs this rung both of the two ladder files `CLIMB-BATCH-1.md` names for it. `ExceptionScoping.fss:31` writes `Nothing[\ZZ32\].get` and `oddJuxt.fss:22,24` write `Nothing[\ZZ32\]`; both now fail with "Unexpected type for a singleton object reference" instead of "Function Nothing is not defined" (§7). Neither passes. The cascade the rung was chosen for is unaffected, because it runs on `Maybe` in type position and `Just(x)` in expression position, which both spellings serve: `HeapTest.fss` and `IntMapTest.fss` lose "Maybe is undefined" and move to their next wall, and `maybeTest.fss` and `naturalsTest.fss` move past `Nothing` and `Just` to `NOTIN` and `__cond` (§7).

**The alternative and its cost.** Taking the corpus's `Nothing[\T\]` would clear `ExceptionScoping.fss` and `oddJuxt.fss` now and would spare the later library route 27 renames in `List.fss`, `Set.fss`, `Map.fss` and `PureList.fss`. Its cost is that `= Nothing`, the only spelling of a `Maybe` value the prose chapters ever write, would be a static error in the compiler world for good, and the compiler world would be carrying the interpreter's acknowledged workaround for a feature the compiler world does not need the workaround for — it has coercion. The library route is a reserved fork and those files will be rewritten line by line when it opens; `basic-lib/convenience.tex` will not be rewritten. Two ladder files, whose spelling the specification does not sanction, were judged the smaller loss, and they are not lost silently: they become ledger row 329 (§8), which names the spelling, both probes and where the fix lies.

**A second decision, smaller: beside `Option`, not over it.** `Maybe` is a second copy of the `Condition` protocol rather than built on `Option`. Three ways to build it over `Option` were considered. Making `Maybe[\T\]` extend `Option[\T\]` fails because `Option` is declared `comprises { NoneObject[\E19\], Some[\E19\] }` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:650`) and a `comprises` clause is closed, so it would have to be widened — a change to a declared type the prelude already has, which `CLIMB-BATCH-1.md` reserves as a stop. Making `Just`/`NothingObject` wrap a `Some`/`NoneObject` field would put an indirection and an allocation under every method to save one-line bodies. A type alias is not available (`Specification/fortress/preamble.tex:55-96` lists type aliases among the not-yet-supported features). The copy costs 56 lines of one-line bodies in `CompilerLibrary.fss`; that was judged cheaper than any of the three, and it is also what the team's draft does — its `Maybe` extends `Condition[\T\]`, not `Option`.

**A third, smaller still: the commented draft was replaced, not left beside the live code.** `CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229` now holds the live declarations in place of the comment. Leaving the comment beside working declarations of the same names would be a stale second answer in the source, and `explorations/protocol.md` keeps rationale out of the tree. The draft is quoted in full in §3 of this report, so nothing is lost.

## 5. What changed

`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-235` — the commented draft replaced by live declarations: `value trait Maybe[\T extends Any\] extends { Condition[\T\] } comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(_: Nothing)`, `getter isNothing(): Boolean`, `seq(): Maybe[\T\]`, `abstract filter(...)` and a commented `opr SQCAP`; `value object Just[\T extends Any\](x: T)`; `value object NothingObject[\T extends Any\]`; `value object Nothing end`.

`Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:522-582` — the bodies, inserted before the "Making vectors" section so the component's order matches the api's. Member for member the bodies of `Option`, `Some` and `NoneObject` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:1308-1367`) with `Option` replaced by `Maybe`, `Some` by `Just`, `NoneObject` by `NothingObject`, `None` by `Nothing`, plus `getter isNothing(): Boolean = NOT self.holds` in the trait.

`ProjectFortress/library_tests/MaybeRungM.fss`, `MaybeRungM.test` — the test.

## 6. Deviations

1. The specification's single `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] ... where {T extends Object}` (`convenience.tex:49`) becomes `value object NothingObject[\T\] extends Maybe[\T\]` plus `value object Nothing end` plus `coerce(_: Nothing) = NothingObject[\T\]`, because `CodeGen.java:4088` refuses a where clause on an object. Semantics preserved at all three use sites the specification writes (§7, `probes/MaybeCoercionSites.txt`); the spelling `Nothing[\T\]` is not preserved (row 329).
2. The specification writes `object`, this writes `value object`, for `Maybe`, `Just`, `NothingObject` and `Nothing` alike — following `Option` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661`), the interpreter (`FortressLibrary.fss:1306-1341`) and the draft (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`), all three of which make the type a value type. The draft writes plain `object Nothing end`; `value object None end` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:661`) and the team's `GenTest4.fss:454` write `value`, and `value` was taken.
3. The specification's `object Just[\T\](just: T)` names the field `just`; this names it `x`, after `value object Some[\E20\](x: E20)` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:657`), the draft's `Just[\T\](x:T)` (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:223`) and the interpreter's `Just[\T\](x:T)` (`FortressLibrary.fss:1312`). Three precedents against one, and the field is not read by name from outside.
4. The specification's `isNothing: Boolean` is a field declaration in a trait; this writes `getter isNothing(): Boolean`, the form every member of `Condition` and `Option` is written in (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:622-655`) and the form `exceptions.tex:122` itself expands the `settable message: Maybe[\String\]` of `:68` into.
5. `Maybe` extends `Condition[\T\]`, which `convenience.tex:46` does not; the draft (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:217`), the interpreter (`FortressLibrary.fss:1307`) and `Option` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649`) all do, and it is what makes a `for` over a `Maybe` work.
6. The specification's `excludes Just[\T\]` on `Nothing` is not written, and neither is any `excludes` clause; `Option` has none either (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661`), and the exclusion is implied by the closed `comprises` clause.
7. `opr SQCAP` is declared as a comment, not live — as on `Option` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:652`) and in the draft (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:220`). It is the interpreter's semilattice meet (`FortressLibrary.fss:1309`); no prose chapter declares it on `Maybe` (`grep -rn SQCAP Specification/basic/ Specification/basic-lib/ Specification/advanced-lib/` finds it only as an operator parameter in `advanced-lib/algebraic-constraints.tex`), and `library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss:64-68` has the team's own `SQCAP` assertions commented out.
8. The coercion is declared once, on the trait; the draft declares it twice, on the trait at `CompilerLibrary.fsi:219` and again on `NothingObject` at `:227`. `Option` declares it once (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:651`), and once is what works.
9. `AnyMaybe` (`FortressLibrary.fss:1292`) is not declared, and neither are `UniqueItem`/`NotUnique` (`:1375-1391`). Rung 2 already recorded that the compiler world has no referent for `AnyMaybe` when it ported `HasRank` (`CompilerLibrary.fss:549-551`); `Library/Set.fsi:65` will need it when the library route opens, and that is that fork's work, not this rung's.

## 8. Ledger row

One new row, provisionally **329** (the gather assigns final numbers in manifest order F, M, N, T; another rung of this batch may open one too).

The defect is not in what this rung landed but in the spelling the corpus and the interpreter's prelude share, and the specification settles it: `basic-lib/convenience.tex:49` declares `Nothing` as one non-parametric object, `basic/exceptions.tex:122,124` uses it that way, and `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1339-1340` concedes the point in its own source ("Obviously ought to be a non-parametric singleton when we get where clauses working"). Fifteen files in `ProjectFortress/tests/` and the interpreter-world collections in `Library/` write the parametric form; two of them, `ExceptionScoping.fss:31` and `oddJuxt.fss:22,24`, name nothing else the compile path lacks, so they are the two files that would otherwise pass. The repair is outside this rung twice over: the interpreter cannot express the specification's declaration either (`probes/WhereClauseNothing.txt` records `T is undefined` from both `fortress compile` and `fortress walk`, the naked type variable in the extends clause), and changing corpus files is a reserved fork. The exact text is in `record.md`.

## 9. What was not done

- `opr SQCAP`, `AnyMaybe`, `UniqueItem` and `NotUnique` are not declared (deviations 7 and 9).
- `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:191-215`, the team's commented draft of a compiler-world `Condition`, is left as it is; `CompilerBuiltin` ships the live one and this rung uses that.
- The gate was not run: this batch is gated once by the coordinator after the merge.

#!/bin/bash
# Compile-path ladder, restricted to the files this rung can affect.
#
# A copy of ../run-ladder.sh with two changes: the ladder root and output
# directory are private to this worktree, and the two whole-corpus loops are
# replaced by one driven by subset.txt (corpus<TAB>file per line).
#
# Pushes every interpreter test program (ProjectFortress/tests/*.fss) and every
# file in ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/ through the compiler path
# unchanged and records how far each one gets.
#
# Reproduce:  bash explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/run-subset.sh
# Outputs:    explorations/compile-ladder/raw/<corpus>/<name>.{compile,run}
#             explorations/compile-ladder/results.tsv
#
# The run uses a private cache tree so it never touches default_repository/caches
# (fortress.caches system property + FORTRESS_CACHES env; ProjectProperties.java:283,
# same mechanism the suite uses at build.xml:941-943), and a private java.io.tmpdir
# so the 5.8 MB Rats! temp directory of every grammar-importing run (RatsUtil.java:138-144)
# is swept per file instead of filling the disk.

set -u

source "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../../experiment/env.sh"

LADDER_ROOT="${LADDER_ROOT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp/ladder-maybe}"
export LADDER_CACHES="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-caches"
export LADDER_TMP="$LADDER_ROOT/ladder-tmp"
export FORTRESS_CACHES="$LADDER_CACHES"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx2g -Xss64m -Dfortress.caches=$LADDER_CACHES -Djava.io.tmpdir=$LADDER_TMP"

PRISTINE="$LADDER_ROOT/pristine"
OUT="${OUT:-$FORTRESS_HOME/explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe}"
RAW="$OUT/raw"
TSV="$OUT/results.tsv"

COMPILE_TIMEOUT=120
RUN_TIMEOUT=60
MIN_FREE_KB=512000

mkdir -p "$RAW/tests" "$RAW/not_working_library_tests" "$LADDER_TMP"

disk_guard () {
    local free
    free=$(df -P / | awk 'NR==2{print $4}')
    if [ "$free" -lt "$MIN_FREE_KB" ]; then
        echo "STOP: only ${free} KB free on / (floor ${MIN_FREE_KB} KB)" | tee -a "$OUT/ladder.log"
        exit 2
    fi
    echo "-- disk free ${free} KB, cache $(du -sm "$LADDER_CACHES" | cut -f1) MB"
}

# Step 1: the compiler-world library, in the order repo-internals.md gives.
build_library () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    local f
    for f in LibraryBuiltin/AnyType.fss LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerLibrary.fss ../Library/CompilerAlgebra.fss \
             ../Library/CompilerSystem.fss ; do
        echo "library: $f"
        timeout 600 ../bin/fortress compile "$f" || { echo "LIBRARY BUILD FAILED on $f"; exit 1; }
    done
}

# Step 2: one known-good compiled program must print PASS before the ladder starts.
sanity () {
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1
    timeout 200 ../bin/fortress compile library_tests/Integer1.fss > /dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
    timeout 60 ../bin/fortress run Integer1 2>&1 | grep -q PASS
}

# Keep only the library's own cache entries; a program's entries are never reused.
prune_cache () {
    ( cd "$LADDER_CACHES" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.now"
    ( cd "$PRISTINE" && find . -type f -print ) | sort > "$LADDER_TMP/.keep"
    comm -23 "$LADDER_TMP/.now" "$LADDER_TMP/.keep" | while read -r p; do
        rm -f "$LADDER_CACHES/$p"
    done
}

component_of () {
    # component/api name as declared, which is what `fortress run` wants
    sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*\(component\|api\)[[:space:]]\+\([A-Za-z0-9_.]\+\).*/\2/p' "$1" | head -1
}

run_one () {
    local corpus="$1" path="$2"
    local base name comp crc rrc t0 t1 ct rt
    base=$(basename "$path")
    name="${base%.*}"
    comp=$(component_of "$path")
    [ -n "$comp" ] || comp="$name"

    t0=$(date +%s)
    timeout -k 5 "$COMPILE_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress compile "$path" \
        > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.compile" 2>&1
    crc=$?
    t1=$(date +%s); ct=$((t1-t0))

    rrc=""
    rt=""
    if [ "$crc" -eq 0 ] && [ "${base##*.}" = "fss" ]; then
        t0=$(date +%s)
        timeout -k 5 "$RUN_TIMEOUT" ../bin/fortress run "$comp" \
            > "$RAW/$corpus/$base.run" 2>&1
        rrc=$?
        t1=$(date +%s); rt=$((t1-t0))
    fi

    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' \
        "$corpus" "$base" "$comp" "$crc" "$rrc" "$ct" "$rt" >> "$TSV"
    echo "$corpus/$base crc=$crc rrc=$rrc ${ct}s"
}

main () {
    echo "=== ladder start $(date -Is) ==="
    disk_guard
    if [ ! -d "$PRISTINE" ]; then
        build_library
        rm -rf "$PRISTINE"; cp -a "$LADDER_CACHES" "$PRISTINE"
    fi
    sanity || { echo "SANITY FAILED: library_tests/Integer1 did not print PASS"; exit 1; }
    echo "sanity ok: library_tests/Integer1 compiles and prints PASS"
    prune_cache

    : > "$TSV"
    cd "$FORTRESS_HOME/ProjectFortress" || exit 1

    local n=0 line corpus f
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r corpus f; do
        [ -n "$corpus" ] || continue
        run_one "$corpus" "$corpus/$f"
        n=$((n+1))
        rm -rf "${LADDER_TMP:?}"/fortress*rats
        if [ $((n % 10)) -eq 0 ]; then prune_cache; disk_guard; fi
    done < "$OUT/subset.txt"
    prune_cache
    echo "=== ladder done $(date -Is), $n files ==="
    disk_guard
}

main "$@"

## 1. What was inherited, and what was re-verified

## 2. Where does this fix belong

`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:332` is the `Maybe` row. The governing prose was found instead by grepping the prose chapters, and it is `basic-lib/convenience.tex` (§3). Those three corrections are listed for the coordinator in `record.md`; this rung does not edit the map.

The fix belongs in the library, not in the compiler. `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/WellKnownNames.java:113-115` (`useCompilerLibraries()`) re-points the compile path's implicit prelude at `CompilerLibrary` and `CompilerBuiltin`, so a declaration in either is in scope for every compiled program with no import. `grep -rn` over `compiler/` and `runtimeSystem/` for `Option`, `Some`, `None`, `NoneObject`, `Maybe`, `NothingObject`, `"Just"` and `"Nothing"` finds nothing, so the protocol being copied is special-cased nowhere those two directories reach. Within the library, `Library/CompilerLibrary` (where the team's draft sits) was chosen over `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin` (where `Option` sits), following the draft's location as the brief directs. It works across the component boundary: `CompilerLibrary.fsi:66-103` already declares 18 objects extending `UncheckedException`, which is declared in the other component at `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:711` — exactly the relation `Maybe extends Condition[\T\]` needs, `Condition` being `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:622`. ## 3. The specification

`Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:31-53`, "Convenience Types", is prose under `Specification/basic-lib/`, so it is the standard and not a listing (rule 3). It declares the optional type directly: the trait at `:46-47`, `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` at `:49`, `object Just[\T\](just: T)` at `:51`. The commented source form the LaTeX was rendered from is immediately above at `:37-43` and agrees.

`Specification/basic/exceptions.tex` then uses it twice: `:68-69` declares `settable message: Maybe[\String\]` and `settable chain: Maybe[\Exception\]` on `trait Exception`, and `:122,124` write those fields' defaults as `getter message(): Maybe[\String\] = Nothing` and `getter chain(): Maybe[\Exception\] = Nothing` — a bare, unparameterised `Nothing` where a `Maybe[\String\]` and a `Maybe[\Exception\]` are expected, under the prose at `:112`, "These fields are default to `Nothing`". `:129` repeats the definition: "an optional value *v* is either `Nothing` or `Just(v)`".

Two independent prose passages, and they agree: `Nothing` is one non-parametric object, usable as a value at any `Maybe[\T\]`.

## 4. Precedent search: has the team solved this here already, and in how many ways

Five, and they do not all agree.

1. **The interpreter's prelude.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1306-1307`: `value trait Maybe[\T\] extends { AnyMaybe, Condition[\T\], UniqueItem[\T\] }`, `value object Just[\T\](x:T)` at `:1312`, `value object Nothing[\T\]` at `:1342`, `value trait AnyMaybe` at `:1292`; api at `.fsi:829-880`. The empty case is **parametric**, and the source says so under protest, in the comment immediately above the declaration — `FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341`: "Obviously ought to be a non-parametric singleton when we get where clauses working."
2. **The team's draft for this world**, commented out at `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229` in the base commit: `value trait Maybe[\T\] extends Condition[\T\] comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(x: Nothing)`, `value object Just[\T\](x:T)`, `value object NothingObject[\T\]` with a second `coerce(x: Nothing)`, and `object Nothing end`. The empty case is **non-parametric, plus a per-`T` object, joined by a coercion**.
3. **The team's tests of that draft**, all in `ProjectFortress/not_working_library_tests/`, which `explorations/coordinator/map/test-coverage.md:32` records as gated by nothing: seven components, shape 2 in every one — `GenTest3.fss:29-38`, `GenTest4.fss:423-454`, `HelperTest1.fss:231-298`, `HelperTest2.fss:231-298`, `HelperTest3.fss:231-298`, `MaybeTest1.fss:22-83`, `MaybeTest2.fss:29-41`. `GenTest4.fss:454` writes `value object Nothing end`; `MaybeTest1.fss:83` and the three `HelperTest*.fss:298` write `object Nothing`.
4. **The shipped `Option`**, `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661`, bodies `.fss:1308-1367`: shape 2 exactly, under the names `Option`, `Some`, `NoneObject`, `None`; complete, in every compiled program's prelude, and the only one of the five known to work. No gated corpus names it (`grep -rn` over `compiler_tests/`, `other_compiler_tests/` and `library_tests/` finds only the English word "None" in three `Compiled12.*` files), so `probes/OptionCoercion.fss` measured it before it was copied: `empty: Option[\ZZ32\] = None` compiles, links and runs, `probes/OptionCoercion.txt` recording `empty=None full=Some(7)` and `PASS`.
5. **The syntax-abstraction machinery, in Java** — which the earlier attempt and the brief both missed, because the brief's grep scope was `compiler/` and `runtimeSystem/` and this is in neither. `syntax_abstractions/phases/TemplateVarRewriter.java:114-117` builds, for a grammar template variable of option depth, an **unqualified** `Maybe[\X\]` trait type (`NodeFactory.makeId(span, "Maybe")`), and `syntax_abstractions/util/FortressTypeToJavaType.java:50-58` maps the name texts `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing`, each with exactly one type argument, to the Java `Option<arg>`. `FortressTypeToJavaTypeJUTest.java:60-94` is that mapping's unit test, and the interpreter's `Evaluator.java:595` tests a typecase clause's type name against `"Just"`.

   These are name texts resolved against the implicit prelude, so before this rung an option-depth gap produced a reference to an undeclared `Maybe` on the compile path, and now it resolves — the direction the design intends, since the name was chosen for the interpreter prelude's `Maybe`. It cannot be broken by this rung's declaration: `FortressTypeToJavaType` only reads the name and the argument count, and `Maybe[\T extends Any\]` takes exactly the one argument that code expects (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:221`). Its `Just` and `Nothing` clauses are unreachable in this tree — the sole producer, `TemplateVarRewriter`, emits only `List` and `Maybe`. And it cannot reach the gate: `grep -rln 'grammar '` over `compiler_tests/`, `other_compiler_tests/` and `library_tests/` finds no file, so no gated compile-path test declares or imports a grammar at all. Recorded as a fact rather than acted on.

The corpus is a sixth voice and not a solution: every use of the name in `ProjectFortress/tests/` and the `*_tests/` directories writes the parametric `Nothing[\T\]` — `tests/ExceptionScoping.fss:31` writes `Nothing[\ZZ32\].get` and `tests/oddJuxt.fss:22,24` write `Nothing[\ZZ32\]`, both in expression position — and so do the interpreter-world collections the later library route would port, `Library/List.fss`, `Set.fss`, `Map.fss`, `PureList.fss` and `QuickCheck.fss`/`.fsi`. Outside shapes 2 and 3 there is no use of an unparameterised `Nothing` as a value anywhere in the tree.

**Competing declarations** (step 6 of the order of work). `grep -rn -E '^\s*(value\s+)?(trait|object)\s+(Maybe|Just|Nothing|NothingObject|AnyMaybe)\b'` over `ProjectFortress/tests/`, every `*_tests/` directory, `not_passing_yet/` and `long_term_not_working/` finds 26 lines, all of them the seven ungated `not_working_library_tests/` components of shape 3. The one gated file in this area is `library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss`, gated through `library_tests/MaybeGetter.test:10` (`tests= Getter1 Getter2 MaybeTest9`); it declares `TestMaybe`, `TestJust` and `TestNothingObject` under prefixed names (`:19,31,43`) and is untouched, as is the ungated `other_compiler_tests/MaybeTest15a.fss`, which uses the same prefixed names. The seven ungated components gain one ambiguity error each ("Type name may refer to: Maybe, CompilerLibrary.Maybe"), which is the error `GenTest3` already gets for `Generator` and `Condition` (`explorations/compile-ladder/after/raw/not_working_library_tests/GenTest3.fss.compile:1-10`); all seven already fail well before reaching it.

Shape 4 was copied member for member, because it is the one that runs. The names and the empty case's shape were taken from shape 2, because it is the team's decision for this world and it agrees with the specification.

## 5. The decision

**The specification's spelling of the empty case was taken, not the corpus's**: `Maybe[\T\] comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(_: Nothing) = NothingObject[\T\]` and a separate `value object Nothing end`. This was a decision, and the code did not force it.

**The two candidates cannot coexist, measured.** `probes/DualNothing.fss` declares both spellings of one name in one scope under local names — `value object NothingD[\T extends Any\] extends MaybeD[\T\]` and then `value object NothingD end`. `probes/DualNothing.txt`: the non-parametric declaration takes the name, and both the parametric declaration's own header (`:16`) and the `comprises` clause that mentions it (`:8`) become errors — "Incorrect number of static arguments for type 'NothingD': provided 1, expected 0". So the fork is binary and there is no overload that serves both spellings.

**Why the specification cannot simply be transcribed.** `probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss` is `convenience.tex:49` under local names — `object NothingW extends MaybeW[\T\] where {T extends Object}`. `probes/WhereClauseNothing.txt` records the same single error from `fortress compile` and from `fortress walk`, both rc=255: `T is undefined`, at the `T` inside the extends clause. Name resolution does not let a where clause bind a type variable used in an extends clause, on either path, so neither implementation can express the declaration the specification writes; `CodeGen.java:4088` (`forObjectDeclPrePass`, `header.getWhereClause().isNone()`) would refuse it at codegen even if name resolution admitted it. The compensating mechanism is coercion, which the compile path has and the interpreter does not (`explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:288`: "nothing: no occurrence of `Coercion` or `coerce` anywhere under `interpreter/`"). That is why the team's draft for this world spells the empty case as it does and the interpreter's prelude does not: the interpreter had no way to write it, and said so at `FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341`.

**What decided it.** Three things point one way. The prose says `Nothing` is one object (`convenience.tex:49`) and uses it as a value at a `Maybe[\String\]` (`exceptions.tex:122`). The team, writing for *this* world, chose that shape (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`) and used it in all seven of its own draft tests. And the interpreter's own author records that the parametric form is a workaround for a missing feature, not the design. The compiler world has the compensating feature, and `probes/MaybeCoercionSites.txt` records it working in all three positions the specification writes an unparameterised `Nothing` in — a declared-type binding, a getter's default, a function argument — with `typecase` confirming the coerced value is a `NothingObject[\ZZ32\]` at run time. Against that stands corpus usage, which is evidence of what was written, not of what the language is (rule 4).

**The alternative and its cost.** Taking the corpus's `Nothing[\T\]` would clear `ExceptionScoping.fss` and `oddJuxt.fss` now — both name nothing else the compile path lacks — and would spare the later library route the renames in `List.fss`, `Set.fss`, `Map.fss` and `PureList.fss`. Its cost is that `= Nothing`, the only spelling of a `Maybe` value the prose chapters ever write, would be a static error in the compiler world for good, and this world would carry the interpreter's acknowledged workaround for a feature it does not need the workaround for. The library route is a reserved fork and those files will be rewritten line by line when it opens; `convenience.tex` will not be rewritten. Two ladder files whose spelling the specification does not sanction were judged the smaller loss, and they are not lost silently: they become the provisional ledger row in `record.md`, which names the spelling, both probes, and where the fix lies.

**A second decision: beside `Option`, not over it.** `Maybe` is a second copy of the `Condition` protocol rather than built on `Option`. Three ways to build it over `Option` were considered and rejected. Making `Maybe[\T\]` extend `Option[\T\]` fails because `Option` is declared `comprises { NoneObject[\E19\], Some[\E19\] }` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:650`) and a `comprises` clause is closed, so it would have to be widened — a change to a declared type the prelude already has, which `CLIMB-BATCH-1.md` reserves as a stop. Making `Just`/`NothingObject` wrap a `Some`/`NoneObject` field would put an indirection and an allocation under every method to save one-line bodies. A type alias is not available: `Specification/fortress/preamble.tex:81` lists type aliases among the features not yet supported. The copy costs 56 lines of one-line bodies in `CompilerLibrary.fss`; that was judged cheaper than any of the three, and it is also what the team's draft does — its `Maybe` extends `Condition[\T\]`, not `Option`.

**A third, smaller: the commented draft was replaced, not left beside the live code.** `CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229` now holds live declarations in place of the comment. Leaving the comment beside working declarations of the same names would be a stale second answer in the source, and `explorations/protocol.md` keeps rationale out of the tree. The draft is quoted in full in §4 of this report and recoverable at `git show cb242a2d8:Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi`, so nothing is lost.

## 6. What changed

`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-235` — the commented draft replaced by live declarations: `value trait Maybe[\T extends Any\] extends { Condition[\T\] } comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(_: Nothing)`, `getter isNothing(): Boolean`, `seq(): Maybe[\T\]`, `abstract filter(f: T -> Condition[\()\]): Maybe[\T\]` and a commented `opr SQCAP`; `value object Just[\T extends Any\](x: T)`; `value object NothingObject[\T extends Any\]`; `value object Nothing end`. `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss:522-582` — the bodies, inserted before the "Making vectors" section so the component's order matches the api's. `ProjectFortress/library_tests/MaybeRungM.fss`, `MaybeRungM.test` — the test. It constructs both cases through a function of a run-time `Boolean` so a body returning a constant would not pass; writes the empty case a second time as `coerced: Maybe[\ZZ32\] = Nothing`; and checks `holds`, `isNothing`, `size`, `get`, `getDefault` with and without a default, `NotFound` thrown by `get` on the empty case, `cond`, `typecase`, a `for` over all three values, `reduce`, and `asString`. The `.test` file is `tests=MaybeRungM` / `link` / `run` / `run_out_contains=PASS` — `_contains`, not the `run_out_WIcontains` that `library_tests/Boolean.test` and `PLAN.md` write and `FileTests.java:147` does not implement.

## 7. Deviations

1. The specification's single `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] ... where {T extends Object}` (`convenience.tex:49`) becomes `value object NothingObject[\T\] extends Maybe[\T\]` plus `value object Nothing end` plus `coerce(_: Nothing) = NothingObject[\T\]`, because that declaration compiles on neither path (`probes/WhereClauseNothing.txt`) and `CodeGen.java:4088` refuses a where clause on an object in any case. The semantics are preserved at all three positions the specification uses the value in (`probes/MaybeCoercionSites.txt`); the spelling `Nothing[\T\]` is not preserved (the ledger row).
2. The specification writes `object`, this writes `value object`, for `Maybe`, `Just`, `NothingObject` and `Nothing` alike — following `Option` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661`), the interpreter (`FortressLibrary.fss:1306-1342`) and the draft (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229`), all three of which make the type a value type. The draft writes plain `object Nothing end` (`:229`); `value object None end` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:661`) and the team's `GenTest4.fss:454` write `value`, and `value` was taken.
3. The specification's `object Just[\T\](just: T)` (`convenience.tex:51`) names the field `just`; this names it `x`, after `value object Some[\E20 extends Any\](x: E20)` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:657`), the draft's `Just[\T\](x:T)` (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:223`) and the interpreter's `Just[\T\](x:T)` (`FortressLibrary.fss:1312`). Three precedents against one, and the field is not read by name from outside.
4. The specification's `isNothing: Boolean` (`convenience.tex:47`) is a field declaration in a trait; this writes `getter isNothing(): Boolean`, the form every member of `Condition` and `Option` is written in (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:622-655`) and the form `exceptions.tex:122` itself expands the `settable message: Maybe[\String\]` of `:68` into.

7. `opr SQCAP` is declared as a comment, not live — as on `Option` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:652`) and in the draft (`CompilerLibrary.fsi:220`). It is the interpreter's semilattice meet (`FortressLibrary.fss:1309`); no prose chapter declares it on `Maybe` (`grep -rn SQCAP Specification/basic/ Specification/basic-lib/ Specification/advanced-lib/` finds it only as an operator parameter in `advanced-lib/algebraic-constraints.tex`), and `library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss:66-68` has the team's own `SQCAP` assertions commented out.

# R1: the record

## FACTS.md

Five lines. The first is the rung; the next three are facts it established on the way; the
fifth is the repair round.

> A mutable variable declared at the top level of a component is stored in a transactional cell on the compiled path: its singleton field is `ACC_FINAL` and holds a `MutableFValue`, reads and writes route through `Transaction.TXRead`/`TXWrite` while a transaction is running, and a nested code-generation context captures the cell rather than a copy of the value (`VarCodeGen.MutableStaticBinding`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java:310-399`; `CodeGen.java:5872-5906`, `:4647-4650`, `:5908-5951`). Rung 3 (`4d419c9e8`) had emitted a bare `GETSTATIC`/`PUTSTATIC` on a non-final field, so such a variable was outside the transaction that `atomic do … end` really does start — against `Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:38-42` — and a write from inside a `for` body or a parallel `do … also` arm was lost outright, at one thread as well as at four. Repaired 2026-09-19 by R1 of the repair batch; gated by `compiler_tests/MutableTopLevelVarInLoop` and `AtomicTopLevelObjectVar`, both deterministic and both failing at one thread on the tree each of them guards, and by `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelVar` under contention. **The bound**: this is `atomic` in a function body or a loop body. As the trailing expression of a `do … also` arm the generated class does not verify at all, before the repair or after (`VerifyError: Inconsistent stackmap frames`, ledger row 322), so "a top-level mutable variable is in the transaction" must not be read as "`atomic` on a top-level mutable variable works". Three defects the rung repairs beyond its own subject, each measured on the base tree and after: a top-level mutable variable assigned from inside an `fn` expression body was silently lost (`probes/skeptic/SK2Closure.fss`: base `g = 0`, landed `g = 7`); a *local* mutable variable of type `String` assigned inside `atomic` failed the verifier (`SK16LocalString.fss`: base `VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack`, landed `st = a b`); and a two-location invariant inside one transaction now holds under contention (`SK8Swap.fss`: base at four threads `x = 9692 y = -8877 sum = 815` against an invariant of 1000, landed PASS).

> **The gate's thread count is inherited from the shell, and this repository pins it to one.** The chain is: the `fastTrack` macro that runs `compiler_tests` sets `FORTRESS_CACHES` and no thread count and no `newenvironment` (`build.xml:927-953`), so the forked JUnit JVM inherits the ambient environment; the harness runs each program in a further subprocess that inherits again (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:480-486`); and `FortressExecutable.getNumThreads` reads `FORTRESS_THREADS` first and only falls back to the processor count or `floor(n/2)` when it is unset (`:37-44`). `experiment/env.sh:6` exports `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, every rung brief tells the agent to source it, and `explorations/coordinator/iteration-cost.md:126` records that no run in the climb used anything else — so in the gate as this project runs it, `compiler_tests` gets one worker. Measured consequence: `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelVar` passes on the *unrepaired* base tree at one thread (`compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/skeptic/skeptic-basetree.txt`, `BASE run AtomicTopLevelVar THREADS=1 :: PASS`), so it is vacuous there and the two deterministic tests are what carry R1. The `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` in the `testSystem` shards (`build.xml:1184`) is a second, explicit pin on a corpus this does not concern. A concurrency defect on the compiled path is therefore **not** gateable by a concurrent test as the gate stands; it is gateable only by a test that fails at one thread. (This line replaces the claim R1 first offered, that `compiler_tests` runs with more than one worker: the chain was right as far as it went and stopped one line short of `getNumThreads`'s first statement.)

> `run_out_WIcontains` is not implemented by the test harness. `FileTests.generalTestFailed` implements six checks — `_contains` (`FileTests.java:147`), `_does_not_contain` (`:155`), `_matches` (`:163`), `_WImatches` (`:171`), `_WCIequals` (`:180`) and `_equals` (`:190`) — and no `_WIcontains` among them, so the sixteen `.test` files that still use it assert only the default "stdout contains pass or PASS" that applies when no check matched (`FileTests.java:266-272`). Nothing is silently unchecked, but the line does nothing. Eight of the sixteen are the last climb's own new tests, because the rung briefs name `library_tests/Boolean.test` as the format to copy and that file carries the inert line; the next brief should name a file that does not. R1's three tests use `run_out_contains=PASS` and `run_out_does_not_contain=FAIL`, the form fifteen `.test` files already used.

> The compiled world's mutable-variable cell holds `fortress.AnyType.Any`, the language's top type, not `runtimeValues.FValue`: `FValue` is an abstract class (`runtimeValues/FValue.java:13`) and a compiled closure is not one of its subclasses, so a mutable variable of arrow type failed the verifier. The defect was already in the tree for *local* mutable variables, which have always been stored in such a cell (`compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/P15LocalArrow.fss`, `P16LocalArrowTask.fss`: `VerifyError` on `49ee5e91`, `f(1) = 3` after R1), and R1 fixed both kinds by widening the payload (`runtimeValues/MutableFValue.java:18-32`, `runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:20,27-28,144,152,226`).

> **The transaction runtime built twenty-two of its twenty-three disabled debug messages eagerly, and on the transactional path that was a crash, not only a cost.** `Transaction.java` has fourteen `debug(` call sites and `BaseTask.java` nine; each concatenated its argument before `debug(String)` tested the flag, except `BaseTask.java:248`, which rung 0 of this same climb had already guarded. Once R1 routed a top-level mutable variable's accesses through the transaction, a twelve-line single-threaded program that ran on `49ee5e91` died (`probes/skeptic/SK25ObjNoAtomicVsAtomic.fss`, frames in `sk25-recursion-entry.txt`). All twenty-three call sites now carry the `if (debug)` guard, twenty-two of them applied in R1's repair round (2026-09-19) in the idiom `BaseTask.java:248` already used, and the case is gated by `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelObjectVar`, whose object type deliberately declares no `asString`. The per-access cost this removes is the mechanism ledger row 302 measured at about 34 % of a 156× gap: inside a transaction each read and write had been building a discarded string of the value (`Transaction.java:162,166,227`), each commit rendering both hash tables (`:232`) and every entry (`:249`), and `BaseTask.getCurrentTransaction` (`:234`) a `Thread` on every call.

Row 324 is not in the judge's instruction list: a probe this round added to replace a speculation with a measurement found it, and the brief's fourth case requires the row.

# M: the record

## FACTS.md

Four lines. The first is the rung; the other three are facts it established on the way. The
first belongs in the compile-path ladder section, the other three wherever the prelude and
the map are discussed.

> **The compiler prelude has `Maybe` since 2026-09-19, and its empty case follows the specification rather than the interpreter.** `value trait Maybe[\T extends Any\] extends { Condition[\T\] } comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] }` with `coerce(_: Nothing)`, plus `value object Just[\T\](x: T)`, `value object NothingObject[\T\]` and a non-parametric `value object Nothing end` (`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-234`, bodies `.fss:522-580`), in place of the team's draft that had been commented out at those same lines. Gated by `ProjectFortress/library_tests/MaybeRungM.test`. **The empty case is the fork this rung decided**: the specification declares `Nothing` as one non-parametric object (`Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:49`, a prose chapter) and uses it as a value at a `Maybe[\String\]` (`basic/exceptions.tex:122,124`, `= Nothing`), which works here only because the compile path has coercion and the interpreter does not; the interpreter's parametric `value object Nothing[\T\]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1342`) is a workaround its own source calls one ("Obviously ought to be a non-parametric singleton when we get where clauses working", `:1340-1341`), and all 22 corpus files and the interpreter-world collections in `Library/` write that parametric form. Consequence: `Nothing[\ZZ32\]` is now "Unexpected type for a singleton object reference" on the compile path, so the two ladder files this rung was assigned, `tests/ExceptionScoping.fss` and `tests/oddJuxt.fss`, do not pass — that cost is the new ledger row. What the rung does deliver is the cascade it was chosen for: over the six ladder files whose recorded first error named one of the three names, 58 errors become 22, and `HeapTest.fss` and `IntMapTest.fss` move off `Maybe is undefined` in `Library/Heap.fsi:54` and `IntMap.fsi:33` to their next wall.

> **One Fortress scope cannot hold both spellings of an optional type's empty case, and the non-parametric declaration wins the name silently.** Declaring `value object NothingD[\T extends Any\] extends MaybeD[\T\]` and then `value object NothingD end` in one component does not raise a duplicate-name error: the name resolves with zero static parameters, and it is the *parametric* declaration's own header and the `comprises` clause naming it that become errors — "Incorrect number of static arguments for type 'NothingD': provided 1, expected 0" (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/DualNothing.fss`, `.txt`). So an optional type's empty case is a binary choice, with no overload that serves both spellings, and a tree that mixes them fails at the parametric uses rather than at the declarations.

> **The specification's own declaration of `Nothing` compiles on neither path, and the reason is name resolution, not codegen.** `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` (`Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:49`) gives the identical single error from `fortress compile` and from `fortress walk`, both rc=255: `T is undefined`, at the `T` inside the extends clause (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss`, `.txt`). A where clause on an object declaration does not bind a type variable used in that declaration's extends clause in either implementation. `CodeGen.forObjectDeclPrePass` would refuse the declaration a second time at codegen — `header.getWhereClause().isNone()` is one of its `canCompile` conditions (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4088`) — but nothing reaches it. This is the mechanism behind `FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341`'s "when we get where clauses working", and it is why both worlds must spell the empty case some other way.

> **`Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing` are named from Java after all, in `syntax_abstractions/`, which is outside the `compiler/` + `runtimeSystem/` scope the climb has been grepping.** `syntax_abstractions/phases/TemplateVarRewriter.java:114-117` builds an **unqualified** `Maybe[\X\]` trait type for a grammar template variable of option depth (`NodeFactory.makeId(span, "Maybe")`), and `syntax_abstractions/util/FortressTypeToJavaType.java:50-58` maps the name texts `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing`, each with exactly one type argument, to the Java `Option<arg>`; `FortressTypeToJavaTypeJUTest.java:60-94` is that mapping's unit test, and the interpreter's `Evaluator.java:595` compares a typecase clause's type name against `"Just"`. Being unqualified, they resolve against whatever `WellKnownNames.useCompilerLibraries()` points the prelude at (`WellKnownNames.java:113-115`), so before this rung an option-depth gap referred to an undeclared `Maybe` on the compile path and now it resolves — the direction the design intends, since the name was chosen for the interpreter prelude's `Maybe`. It cannot break: that code reads only the name text and the argument count, and `Maybe[\T extends Any\]` takes the one argument it expects. It also cannot reach the gate: `grep -rln 'grammar '` over `compiler_tests/`, `other_compiler_tests/` and `library_tests/` finds no file, so no gated compile-path test declares or imports a grammar. **The general lesson for later rungs**: "nothing in Java or Scala names this" must be grepped over `src/com/sun/fortress/` and not over `compiler/` and `runtimeSystem/` alone.

**One new row**, proposed for section 10 (Bytecode-compiler path) after the repair batch's rows, numbered **329** if F proposes none; the gather assigns final numbers in manifest order F, M, N, T.

The ladder subset before and after is in `compile-ladder/rung-maybe/ladder-before/` and `ladder-after/`: these two files keep one error each and change which one, while the other four in the subset lose 56 of their 58. |

**No appends to existing rows.** The two candidates were considered and neither needs one. Row 71 and row 138, which `spec-to-implementation.md:332` gives as the `Maybe` row's ledger citations, are about the compiler prelude's absent declarations as a class rather than about this name, and the FACTS line above is where this rung's addition belongs; nothing either row claims has become false.

## Three map corrections, offered separately

Not folded by this rung, since `explorations/coordinator/map/` is the coordinator's. `explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:332`, the `Maybe` row, has three: it gives the commented compiler-world draft as `CompilerLibrary.fsi:194-204`, where the base commit `cb242a2d8` has it at `:217-229` (and `FACTS.md:79` gives the same block a third span, `:168-204`); it gives `Option` as `CompilerBuiltin.fsi:648-660`, where it is at `:649-661`; and its spec column names `library/default-libraries.tex`, an api rendering, where the governing prose is `basic-lib/convenience.tex:31-53`. The row's status, "present … but **wholly commented out**", is what this rung changes.

## The handover state line

> Rung M of climb batch 1 is on `wip/rung-maybe` (base `cb242a2d8`): the compiler prelude now declares `Maybe[\T\]`, `Just[\T\]`, `NothingObject[\T\]` and a non-parametric `Nothing` in `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-234` with bodies at `.fss:522-580`, replacing the team's commented draft at those lines and copying the shipped `Option`/`Some`/`NoneObject`/`None` member for member. Gated by `ProjectFortress/library_tests/MaybeRungM.test`, which links and runs to `PASS` (`OK (2 tests)`) from a bytecode cache wiped and rebuilt from scratch in library order. The rung was relaunched after an earlier attempt of it had pushed three milestones to the same branch; that work was verified rather than redone, and four things it had wrong are corrected in its report — it had missed that `syntax_abstractions/` names all three of these types in Java, had argued rather than measured that the two spellings of the empty case cannot coexist, had mis-attributed the inexpressibility of the specification's declaration to codegen rather than to name resolution, and had mis-added its own error counts. **The decision the batch owes Pavol**: the empty case follows `Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:49` and the team's own draft for this world (non-parametric `Nothing`, coerced) and not the interpreter and the corpus (parametric `Nothing[\T\]`), so the two ladder files the rung was assigned, `ExceptionScoping.fss` and `oddJuxt.fss`, do **not** pass and the spelling they use is now a static error on the compile path; the alternative and its cost are argued in `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/REPORT.md` §5, and the cost is the rung's one verified ledger row (provisionally 329). The cascade the rung was chosen for did land: 58 errors to 22 over the six ladder files that named these types, with `HeapTest.fss` and `IntMapTest.fss` off `Maybe is undefined` inside `Library/Heap.fsi` and `IntMap.fsi`. `Option`, `Some`, `NoneObject` and `None` are untouched, as is the prefixed `library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss` that rung 1 lost a cycle to. > **One Fortress scope cannot hold both spellings of an optional type's empty case, and the non-parametric declaration wins the name silently.** Declaring `value object NothingD[\T extends Any\] extends MaybeD[\T\]` and then `value object NothingD end` in one component does not raise a duplicate-name error: the name resolves with zero static parameters, and it is the *parametric* declaration's own header and the `comprises` clause naming it that become errors — "Incorrect number of static arguments for type 'NothingD': provided 1, expected 0" (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/DualNothing.fss`, `.txt`). > **The specification's own declaration of `Nothing` compiles on neither path, and the reason is name resolution, not codegen.** `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` (`Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:49`) gives the identical single error from `fortress compile` and from `fortress walk`, both rc=255: `T is undefined`, at the `T` inside the extends clause (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-maybe/probes/WhereClauseNothing.fss`, `.txt`). > **`Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing` are named from Java after all, in `syntax_abstractions/`, which is outside the `compiler/` + `runtimeSystem/` scope the climb has been grepping.** `syntax_abstractions/phases/TemplateVarRewriter.java:114-117` builds an **unqualified** `Maybe[\X\]` trait type for a grammar template variable of option depth (`NodeFactory.makeId(span, "Maybe")`), and `syntax_abstractions/util/FortressTypeToJavaType.java:50-58` maps the name texts `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing`, each with exactly one type argument, to the Java `Option<arg>`; `FortressTypeToJavaTypeJUTest.java:60-94` is that mapping's unit test, and the interpreter's `Evaluator.java:595` compares a typecase clause's type name against `"Just"`. Rung M: REPORT.md, record.md, and the re-verification of the inherited attempt

The branch carried three commits from an earlier attempt of this rung, relaunched
after its container died.  That work is verified rather than redone: the bytecode
cache was wiped and rebuilt from scratch in library order, and the test, every
probe, the .test file through the harness and the ladder subset's after half were
all re-run.  Everything reproduced.

Four things the earlier attempt had wrong or missing are corrected here.  It had
no record.md.  Its precedent search concluded that nothing in Java names these
three types, because the scope it grepped was compiler/ and runtimeSystem/;
syntax_abstractions/ names all three (FortressTypeToJavaType.java:50-58,
TemplateVarRewriter.java:114-117), which is benign here and is recorded as a fact.
It argued rather than measured that the two spellings of the empty case cannot
coexist; probes/DualNothing now measures it.  It attributed the inexpressibility
of the specification's own declaration to CodeGen.java:4088 when its own probe
shows name resolution refuses it first, on both paths.  And its error arithmetic
and its guess about the seven ungated components were both wrong; both are now
measured (probes/UngatedAmbiguity.txt).

# Rung M: `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing` for the compiler world

problem: `explorations/compile-ladder/after/raw/tests/oddJuxt.fss.compile:2` — "Function Nothing is not defined."; and "Maybe is undefined." 472 times across 51 files of the same recorded run, more than any other single name, while the compiler prelude declares none of the three.
spec: `Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:46-52` — the Convenience Types section (`:31-53`) of a prose chapter of Part Basic Library declares `trait Maybe[\T\] comprises { Nothing, Just[\T\] }` with `isNothing: Boolean`, `object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object}` and `object Just[\T\](just: T) extends Maybe[\T\]`; used at `Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:122,124`, which write the defaults of two `Maybe` fields as `= Nothing` (the same declarations in comment form at `convenience.tex:37-43` and `exceptions.tex:114,116`).
precedent: `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661` with bodies at `.fss:1308-1367` — the shipped `value trait Option[\E19 extends Any\] extends { Condition[\E19\] } comprises { NoneObject[\E19\], Some[\E19\] }` with `coerce(_: None)` and `value object None end`, which is this protocol under other names and is the shape copied member for member; the team's own commented draft for these names is `Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229` at the base commit.
deviation: nine, each listed in §7 below; the first is that the specification's single non-parametric `Nothing` is realised as `NothingObject[\T\]` plus `value object Nothing end` plus `coerce(_: Nothing)`, because the specification's own declaration compiles on neither path — the naked `T` in its extends clause is "T is undefined" from name resolution (`probes/WhereClauseNothing.txt`) and `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4088` refuses a where clause on an object declaration in any case — while coercion is a mechanism this path has and the interpreter lacks.

## 1. What was inherited, and what was re-verified

This rung was relaunched. The branch `wip/rung-maybe` already carried three pushed commits from an earlier attempt of this same rung — `d5352bd21` (the failing test and one probe), `96aef343d` (the captured pre-edit failure), `f6b4a82e1` (the library edit, four more probes, the subset driver and both ladder runs) — and the worktree held an uncommitted REPORT.md, an uncommitted probe (`WhereClauseNothing`), the two ladder result directories and the earlier attempt's `tmp/` logs. No skeptic had seen any of it.

Committed work was read and re-checked rather than redone. What was re-run in this session, from a bytecode cache **wiped and rebuilt from scratch** in library order (`logs/verify-rebuild.log`: AnyType 27 s, CompilerBuiltin 118 s, CompilerLibrary 33 s, CompilerAlgebra 2 s, CompilerSystem 1 s, all rc=0 — so the edited library is well-formed against an empty cache, not only against an incrementally patched one): the test, every probe, the `.test` file through the harness, and the ladder subset's "after" half. All of the earlier attempt's recorded results reproduced. `logs/verify-probes.log`, `logs/verify-gate-and-ladder.log`.

**Competing declarations** (step 6 of the order of work). `grep -rn -E '^\s*(value\s+)?(trait|object)\s+(Maybe|Just|Nothing|NothingObject|AnyMaybe)\b'` over `ProjectFortress/tests/`, every `*_tests/` directory, `not_passing_yet/` and `long_term_not_working/` finds 26 lines, all of them the seven ungated `not_working_library_tests/` components of shape 3. The one gated file in this area is `library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss`, gated through `library_tests/MaybeGetter.test:10` (`tests= Getter1 Getter2 MaybeTest9`); it declares `TestMaybe`, `TestJust` and `TestNothingObject` under prefixed names (`:19,31,43`) and is untouched, as is the ungated `other_compiler_tests/MaybeTest15a.fss`, which uses the same prefixed names. Rung 1 lost a cycle to this file; this rung does not collide with it. What this rung does to those seven was measured rather than assumed, and the earlier attempt had it wrong both ways (`probes/UngatedAmbiguity.txt`, captures in `logs/ungated/`). Five of them gain **7 to 12** ambiguity errors, not one each — `GenTest3` 6 errors to 13, `GenTest4` 122 to 131, and `HelperTest1`, `HelperTest2` and `HelperTest3` 115 to 127 apiece — every new one of the form "Type name may refer to: Maybe, CompilerLibrary.Maybe" (or `Just`, or `NothingObject`), which is the shape all five already carried for `Generator` and `Condition` against `CompilerBuiltin` (`explorations/compile-ladder/after/raw/not_working_library_tests/GenTest3.fss.compile:1-4`). The other two, `MaybeTest1` and `MaybeTest2`, gain nothing: each dies on a `Syntax Error` at its line 15, before name resolution runs. None of the seven compiles before or after, and none is gated.

Shape 4 was copied member for member, because it is the one that runs. The names and the empty case's shape were taken from shape 2, because it is the team's decision for this world and it agrees with the specification.

input.precedentSearch: Five prior answers in the tree, and they disagree. (1) The interpreter's prelude: value trait Maybe[\T\] at Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1306, Just[\T\](x:T) at :1312, parametric value object Nothing[\T\] at :1342 — and the comment immediately above it, :1340-1341, "Obviously ought to be a non-parametric singleton when we get where clauses working". (2) The team's draft for this world, commented out at Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229: Maybe comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] } with coerce(x: Nothing) and a separate object Nothing end. (3) The team's own tests of that draft, shape 2 in all seven ungated not_working_library_tests/ components (GenTest3:29-38, GenTest4:423-454, HelperTest1/2/3:231-298, MaybeTest1:22-83, MaybeTest2:29-41). (4) The shipped Option/Some/NoneObject/None, CompilerBuiltin.fsi:649-661 with bodies .fss:1308-1367 — shape 2 exactly, complete, in every compiled program's prelude, and the only one of the five known to work; no gated corpus exercises it, so probes/OptionCoercion.fss measured it before it was copied (PASS, empty=None full=Some(7)). (5) The syntax-abstraction machinery in Java, which the brief's grep scope (compiler/, runtimeSystem/) misses: syntax_abstractions/phases/TemplateVarRewriter.java:114-117 builds an unqualified Maybe[\X\] for an option-depth template gap and syntax_abstractions/util/FortressTypeToJavaType.java:50-58 maps the name texts Maybe, Just and Nothing to the Java Option<arg>. Precedent followed: shape 4 copied member for member for the bodies (it is the one that runs), with the names and the empty case's shape from shape 2 (the team's decision for this world, and the one that agrees with the specification). Location followed the draft: Library/CompilerLibrary, not CompilerBuiltin where Option sits — it works across the component boundary, since CompilerLibrary.fsi:66-103 already declares 18 objects extending CompilerBuiltin.fsi:711's UncheckedException, and it rebuilds in 36 s against 181 s.
specCitations: Specification/basic-lib/convenience.tex:46-52 (prose, Part Basic Library) — trait Maybe[\T\] comprises { Nothing, Just[\T\] } with isNothing: Boolean; object Nothing extends Maybe[\T\] excludes Just[\T\] where {T extends Object} at :49; object Just[\T\](just: T) at :51; the section runs :31-53 and the same declarations in comment form are at :37-43
Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:68-69 — settable message: Maybe[\String\] and settable chain: Maybe[\Exception\] on trait Exception

Specification/basic/exceptions.tex:122,124 — getter message(): Maybe[\String\] = Nothing and getter chain(): Maybe[\Exception\] = Nothing, an unparameterised Nothing as a value of a parameterised Maybe (comment form at :114,116; prose at :112 and :129)

Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31 — Part Library "is largely automatically generated from the API code for the libraries themselves", which is why library/default-libraries.tex (the map's spec citation for this row) is not evidence and convenience.tex is
Specification/fortress/preamble.tex:81 — type aliases are among the features not yet supported, which rules out one of the three ways of building Maybe over Option
decisions: The empty case follows the specification and the team's draft (non-parametric value object Nothing plus NothingObject[\T\] plus coerce(_: Nothing) = NothingObject[\T\]), not the interpreter and the corpus (parametric Nothing[\T\]). Alternative rejected: the corpus spelling, which would have cleared both ladder files this rung was assigned (ExceptionScoping.fss and oddJuxt.fss name nothing else the compile path lacks) and spared the later library route the renames in List.fss, Set.fss, Map.fss and PureList.fss — at the price of making `= Nothing`, the only spelling of a Maybe value the prose chapters ever write, a permanent static error in the compiler world, and of carrying the interpreter's self-declared workaround into the one world that has the compensating feature. Decided on convenience.tex:49 plus exceptions.tex:122, the team's own choice for this world at CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229, and FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341 conceding the point against its own code; the cost is the rung's one verified ledger row.

Maybe is a second copy of the Condition protocol beside Option, not built over it. Three alternatives rejected: extending Option[\T\] would require widening its closed comprises clause (CompilerBuiltin.fsi:650), a change to a declared type the prelude already has and a reserved stop; wrapping a Some/NoneObject field would add an indirection and an allocation under every method to save one-line bodies; a type alias is not a supported feature (preamble.tex:81). The copy costs 56 lines of one-line bodies, and it is also what the team's draft does — its Maybe extends Condition[\T\], not Option.

The commented draft at CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229 was replaced rather than left beside the live declarations. Alternative rejected: keeping the comment, which would leave a stale second answer to the same question in the source tree; protocol.md keeps rationale out of the tree, the draft is quoted in full in REPORT.md §4, and it is recoverable at git show cb242a2d8:Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi.

Option, Some, NoneObject and None were left entirely untouched, as were the prefixed TestMaybe/TestJust/TestNothingObject of the gated library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss. Alternative rejected: renaming Option to Maybe so one implementation serves both, which would remove declarations a gated test uses — a reserved stop.

The test was given run_out_does_not_contain=FAIL in addition to run_out_contains=PASS. Alternative rejected: the single check the brief requires; the harness implements six checks at FileTests.java:147,155,163,171,180,190 and 22 .test files already carry the second one, so adding it costs nothing and closes the case where a later edit makes the component print FAIL and stop.
divergences: The corpus spelling Nothing[\ZZ32\] in expression position (tests/ExceptionScoping.fss:31, tests/oddJuxt.fss:22,24) runs under walk and is now "Unexpected type for a singleton object reference" compiled. The specification favours the COMPILED side: basic-lib/convenience.tex:49 declares Nothing as one non-parametric object and basic/exceptions.tex:122,124 use it as an unparameterised value. The defect is therefore in the corpus and in the interpreter's prelude, and the repair is outside this rung twice over (changing corpus files is a reserved fork; and the specification's declaration cannot be written in either implementation, so the interpreter cannot simply be corrected to match). Landed with a verified ledger row, provisionally 329 — the fourth case the brief names.

The specification's spelling `= Nothing` at a declared Maybe type compiles, links and runs on the compiled path (probes/MaybeCoercionSites.txt: a declared-type binding, a getter's default, a function argument, all PASS, with typecase confirming the coerced value is a NothingObject[\ZZ32\] at run time) and cannot work under walk, which has no coercion at all (map/spec-to-implementation.md:288). The specification favours the COMPILED side; this is the rung's positive result and needs no row, since the interpreter's absence of coercion is already on record.

Not a divergence, checked and found to agree: the specification's own declaration of Nothing (convenience.tex:49) is refused identically by both paths — "T is undefined" at the T inside the extends clause, rc=255 from fortress compile and from fortress walk (probes/WhereClauseNothing.txt). Name resolution refuses it before codegen; CodeGen.java:4088 would refuse the where clause a second time. This is the mechanism behind FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341.
notDone: opr SQCAP is declared as a comment only, following Option (CompilerBuiltin.fsi:652) and the draft (CompilerLibrary.fsi:220). No prose chapter declares it on Maybe (grep over Specification/basic/, basic-lib/, advanced-lib/ finds it only as an operator parameter in advanced-lib/algebraic-constraints.tex), and the team's own SQCAP assertions in library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss:66-68 are commented out.

AnyMaybe (FortressLibrary.fss:1292), UniqueItem (:1380) and NotUnique (:1388) are not declared. Library/Set.fsi:65 will need AnyMaybe when the library route opens; rung 2 already recorded the compiler world's lack of a referent for it.
Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:191-215, the team's commented draft of a compiler-world Condition, is left as it is; CompilerBuiltin.fsi:621 ships the live one and this rung uses that.

Nothing was acted on in syntax_abstractions/, where the three names are referenced from Java. It cannot break (that code reads only the name text and the argument count, and Maybe[\T extends Any\] takes the one argument it expects) and it cannot reach the gate (no gated compile-path corpus declares or imports a grammar), so it is recorded as a fact for later rungs instead.

The gate was not run: the batch is gated once by the coordinator after the merge. library_tests/MaybeRungM.test was run through the harness on its own (OK (2 tests)), which is the gate's own mechanism over the one new file.

The ladder subset's "before" half was not re-run this session — it needs the base library checked back in and the private cache rebuilt twice more. It is corroborated instead by the independently recorded shared baseline at explorations/compile-ladder/after/raw/tests/, which gives the same first error and the same error count for all six files.

Three corrections to explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md:332 are offered in record.md rather than applied, since the map is the coordinator's: the draft's location (:194-204 given, :217-229 actual, and FACTS.md:79 gives a third span :168-204), Option's location (:648-660 given, :649-661 actual), and the spec column naming an api rendering where the governing prose is basic-lib/convenience.tex.
input.summary:
The rung landed. The compiler prelude now declares value trait Maybe[\T extends Any\] extends { Condition[\T\] } comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] } with coerce(_: Nothing), plus Just, NothingObject and a non-parametric value object Nothing, at Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-234 with bodies at .fss:522-580 — in place of the team's draft that had been commented out at those same lines, and copied member for member from the shipped Option/Some/NoneObject/None. Gated by ProjectFortress/library_tests/MaybeRungM.test.

The branch was relaunched: it already carried three pushed commits from an earlier attempt of this same rung, plus an uncommitted report and probes. That work was verified rather than redone — the bytecode cache was wiped and rebuilt from scratch, and the test, every probe, the .test file through the harness and the after-ladder run were all re-run, all reproducing. Four things the earlier attempt had wrong are corrected and now measured: it concluded nothing in Java names these three types, having grepped only compiler/ and runtimeSystem/, while syntax_abstractions/ names all three (benign here, and no gated compile-path test declares a grammar); it asserted rather than measured that the two spellings of the empty case cannot coexist; it attributed the inexpressibility of the specification's own declaration to codegen when name resolution refuses it first, on both paths; and both its error arithmetic and its guess about the seven ungated components were wrong.

The decision the batch owes Pavol: the empty case follows convenience.tex:49 and the team's draft, not the interpreter and the corpus. So Nothing[\ZZ32\] is now a static error on the compile path and the two ladder files assigned to this rung do not pass. That was chosen with the alternative costed, and it is the rung's one verified ledger row (provisionally 329). The cascade the rung was chosen for did land: over the six ladder files that named these types, 58 errors become 22, with HeapTest and IntMapTest off "Maybe is undefined" inside Library/Heap.fsi and IntMap.fsi. Option, Some, NoneObject, None and the prefixed names of the gated MaybeTest9 are untouched. No .java or .scala changed. Five commits pushed to wip/rung-maybe; working tree clean.

(5) The syntax-abstraction machinery in Java, which the brief's grep scope (compiler/, runtimeSystem/) misses: syntax_abstractions/phases/TemplateVarRewriter.java:114-117 builds an unqualified Maybe[\X\] for an option-depth template gap and syntax_abstractions/util/FortressTypeToJavaType.java:50-58 maps the name texts Maybe, Just and Nothing to the Java Option<arg>. Precedent followed: shape 4 copied member for member for the bodies (it is the one that runs), with the names and the empty case's shape from shape 2 (the team's decision for this world, and the one that agrees with the specification). decisions: The empty case follows the specification and the team's draft (non-parametric value object Nothing plus NothingObject[\T\] plus coerce(_: Nothing) = NothingObject[\T\]), not the interpreter and the corpus (parametric Nothing[\T\]). Alternative rejected: the corpus spelling, which would have cleared both ladder files this rung was assigned (ExceptionScoping.fss and oddJuxt.fss name nothing else the compile path lacks) and spared the later library route the renames in List.fss, Set.fss, Map.fss and PureList.fss — at the price of making `= Nothing`, the only spelling of a Maybe value the prose chapters ever write, a permanent static error in the compiler world, and of carrying the interpreter's self-declared workaround into the one world that has the compensating feature. Decided on convenience.tex:49 plus exceptions.tex:122, the team's own choice for this world at CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229, and FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341 conceding the point against its own code; the cost is the rung's one verified ledger row.

Three alternatives rejected: extending Option[\T\] would require widening its closed comprises clause (CompilerBuiltin.fsi:650), a change to a declared type the prelude already has and a reserved stop; wrapping a Some/NoneObject field would add an indirection and an allocation under every method to save one-line bodies; a type alias is not a supported feature (preamble.tex:81). The copy costs 56 lines of one-line bodies, and it is also what the team's draft does — its Maybe extends Condition[\T\], not Option.

The commented draft at CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-229 was replaced rather than left beside the live declarations. Alternative rejected: keeping the comment, which would leave a stale second answer to the same question in the source tree; protocol.md keeps rationale out of the tree, the draft is quoted in full in REPORT.md §4, and it is recoverable at git show cb242a2d8:Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi.

Option, Some, NoneObject and None were left entirely untouched, as were the prefixed TestMaybe/TestJust/TestNothingObject of the gated library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss. The specification favours the COMPILED side: basic-lib/convenience.tex:49 declares Nothing as one non-parametric object and basic/exceptions.tex:122,124 use it as an unparameterised value. The defect is therefore in the corpus and in the interpreter's prelude, and the repair is outside this rung twice over (changing corpus files is a reserved fork; and the specification's declaration cannot be written in either implementation, so the interpreter cannot simply be corrected to match). Landed with a verified ledger row, provisionally 329 — the fourth case the brief names.

The specification favours the COMPILED side; this is the rung's positive result and needs no row, since the interpreter's absence of coercion is already on record.

Not a divergence, checked and found to agree: the specification's own declaration of Nothing (convenience.tex:49) is refused identically by both paths — "T is undefined" at the T inside the extends clause, rc=255 from fortress compile and from fortress walk (probes/WhereClauseNothing.txt). Name resolution refuses it before codegen; CodeGen.java:4088 would refuse the where clause a second time. This is the mechanism behind FortressLibrary.fss:1340-1341.

No prose chapter declares it on Maybe (grep over Specification/basic/, basic-lib/, advanced-lib/ finds it only as an operator parameter in advanced-lib/algebraic-constraints.tex), and the team's own SQCAP assertions in library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss:66-68 are commented out.

data.summary:
The rung landed. The compiler prelude now declares value trait Maybe[\T extends Any\] extends { Condition[\T\] } comprises { Just[\T\], NothingObject[\T\] } with coerce(_: Nothing), plus Just, NothingObject and a non-parametric value object Nothing, at Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:217-234 with bodies at .fss:522-580 — in place of the team's draft that had been commented out at those same lines, and copied member for member from the shipped Option/Some/NoneObject/None. Gated by ProjectFortress/library_tests/MaybeRungM.test.

The branch was relaunched: it already carried three pushed commits from an earlier attempt of this same rung, plus an uncommitted report and probes. That work was verified rather than redone — the bytecode cache was wiped and rebuilt from scratch, and the test, every probe, the .test file through the harness and the after-ladder run were all re-run, all reproducing. Four things the earlier attempt had wrong are corrected and now measured: it concluded nothing in Java names these three types, having grepped only compiler/ and runtimeSystem/, while syntax_abstractions/ names all three (benign here, and no gated compile-path test declares a grammar); it asserted rather than measured that the two spellings of the empty case cannot coexist; it attributed the inexpressibility of the specification's own declaration to codegen when name resolution refuses it first, on both paths; and both its error arithmetic and its guess about the seven ungated components were wrong.

The decision the batch owes Pavol: the empty case follows convenience.tex:49 and the team's draft, not the interpreter and the corpus. So Nothing[\ZZ32\] is now a static error on the compile path and the two ladder files assigned to this rung do not pass. That was chosen with the alternative costed, and it is the rung's one verified ledger row (provisionally 329). The cascade the rung was chosen for did land: over the six ladder files that named these types, 58 errors become 22, with HeapTest and IntMapTest off "Maybe is undefined" inside Library/Heap.fsi and IntMap.fsi. Option, Some, NoneObject, None and the prefixed names of the gated MaybeTest9 are untouched. No .java or .scala changed. Five commits pushed to wip/rung-maybe; working tree clean.
